clue.text: Flower we could cut small twice with a similar result

definitions.text: Flower we could cut small twice with a similar result

parts.words: Flower we could cut small twice with a similar result
parts.note: the word sought names a flower; strike out two of its S letters (S being small) and you are left with another word for flower, a bloom

explanation.surface: A gardener muses that pruning a flower twice would leave it looking much the same.
explanation.walkthrough: 'small' is the usual abbreviation S; remove both S's from the seven-letter word and BLOOM remains, a near-synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: Blossom is the bloom on a fruit tree or shrub, so it names a flower.

clue.text: Bust of Romeo pinched by barbarian

indicators.note: being pinched by something means being gripped inside it, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: a barbarian is a brute or beast
Romeo is R in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A sculpture of the lover Romeo is stolen by a savage raider.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bust' looks like a statue, but it is the chest.
explanation.definitionFit: A bust is a woman's chest, the same body part as the bosom.

clue.text: They produce 4 parts of the body

definitions.meaning: 4-down is MUSIC; church instruments with pipes produce it
the heart, liver and lungs are internal parts of the body

explanation.surface: Things that make music, or the parts inside us.
explanation.definitionFit: Organ is both a keyboard instrument with pipes and a body part such as the heart.

clue.text: Street battle over heartless boy snatching stray food

indicators.note: in a down clue, over says the word battle is turned back to front

parts.note: a battle is a war

indicators.note: snatching means grabbing hold of, so the shortened boy wraps around the next piece
heartless says the middle letter is taken out of the word boy

parts.note: taken as written before its centre is removed
to stray is to err, to wander off course

explanation.surface: A street fight breaks out when a cruel lad seizes a wandering animal's dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stray' looks like a noun for a lost animal but is the verb meaning to wander off course; 'over', 'heartless' and 'snatching' are the indicators.
explanation.definitionFit: A strawberry is a soft red fruit eaten as food.

clue.text: Nothing odd about impulse — itch — to achieve harmony?

indicators.note: taking nothing from the odd positions of impulse and itch leaves only their even letters

explanation.surface: An urge, a mere itch, drives someone to seek harmony.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nothing odd about' discards the first, third, fifth and so on letters of 'impulse itch', keeping the even ones.
explanation.definitionFit: Harmony is pleasing combined sound, so it can stand for music as a whole, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Costs of Queen's son good for Left

indicators.note: one thing put for another means it replaces it, so good takes the place of Left

parts.note: Charles is the son of Queen Elizabeth II

explanation.surface: A report on what the royal prince costs, with a political twist about the Left.
explanation.walkthrough: 'good for Left' swaps the L in CHARLES for a G.
explanation.definitionFit: Charges are fees or prices asked, which are costs.

clue.text: Reconstruction of car held at church

indicators.note: a reconstruction rebuilds something in a new form, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A car crash is restaged for investigators at a church.
explanation.definitionFit: A cathedral is the principal church of a diocese, holding the bishop's seat.

clue.text: Some ground article goes on about twice

parts.note: a is the indefinite article
about gives C (circa) and then again RE (regarding), two versions of the same word

explanation.surface: A newspaper article keeps going on about a plot of land.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' is used twice over: C, short for circa, then RE, meaning concerning.
explanation.definitionFit: An acre is a unit of land area, so a patch of ground.

clue.text: More fancy getting into Gilbert & Sullivan — what must be going down?

indicators.note: getting into something means entering it, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: the operetta pair are commonly shortened to G and S
lacier means more frilly or ornate, trimmed with more lace

explanation.surface: Someone grows fonder of comic opera, and asks what must be on its way down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'what must be going down' is cryptic: ice rivers creep downhill under gravity, so are always descending.
explanation.definitionFit: Glaciers are slow rivers of ice that flow down mountainsides and valleys.

clue.text: Doctor Seuss framing what he might write with anxiety

indicators.note: framing means surrounding, so the shuffled name goes around the next piece
to doctor something is to tamper with it, so the letters of Seuss are rearranged

parts.note: an author writes with a pen

explanation.surface: The children's author Dr Seuss is pictured nervously holding his writing tool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctor' is not his title but the anagram signal on his name, and 'framing' wraps the shuffled name around his writing tool.
explanation.definitionFit: Suspense is the anxious uncertainty of waiting to learn what happens.

clue.text: Enthusiastic in punt with initial change of direction

indicators.note: the first letter, a compass point, is swapped for another compass point: west becomes east

parts.note: a punt is a bet or wager

explanation.surface: Someone keen on a boat trip changes course at the start.
explanation.walkthrough: 'punt' looks like the flat boat, but it means a bet; its first letter W (west) becomes E (east).
explanation.definitionFit: Eager means keen and full of enthusiasm.

clue.text: They come round once a week, unsettling us with arty ads

definitions.text: They come round once a week

indicators.note: unsettling throws things into disorder, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Pretentious adverts that pop up weekly leave us disturbed.
explanation.definitionFit: A particular weekday recurs every seven days, so these days arrive once each week.

clue.text: Squashes that could make a snack

definitions.meaning: squeezes something tightly between two others
fillings between bread slices make a quick light meal

explanation.surface: Crushing things together could produce a quick bite.
explanation.definitionFit: To be squeezed in tightly between two things is to be wedged, and bread-and-filling snacks share that name.

clue.text: Religious education brings in very little money, or 'ready'

indicators.note: bringing something in means taking it inside, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: RE is the school subject Religious Education
1p, one penny, written as IP, is a tiny sum

explanation.surface: Teaching religion earns a pittance, or so a cynic says.
explanation.walkthrough: 'very little money' is 1p, read as the letters IP; RE is the British school subject.
explanation.definitionFit: Fruit that is fully developed and fit for eating is said to be ready.

clue.text: Still in post on a railway

parts.note: a post is a station, a place of duty

explanation.surface: Someone stays at their post beside the railway line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Still' and 'railway' tempt one to think of a train station; it is the adjective meaning motionless.
explanation.definitionFit: Stationary means not moving, so still.

clue.text: Degrees of difference between the seasons?

definitions.text: Degrees of difference between the seasons?

parts.words: Degrees of difference between the seasons?
parts.note: the warmth or cold measured in degrees is what varies from summer to winter

explanation.surface: How much the seasons differ from one another.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Degrees of difference' reads as 'how far apart', but literally it is the readings on a thermometer.
explanation.definitionFit: Measured heat levels, given in degrees, change markedly through the year.

clue.text: After sales talk, study's done up with decorations

parts.note: patter is the rapid persuasive talk of a salesman

indicators.note: in a down clue, up says the word is read from bottom to top, so it is reversed

parts.note: a den is a study; the 's is short for is

explanation.surface: After the salesman's pitch, the study has been redecorated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'done up' looks like redecorating, but 'up' turns DEN into NED.
explanation.definitionFit: Something patterned carries decorative designs, so is adorned with decorations.

clue.text: Rising carbon — I'm about to support green business

definitions.note: used as a modifier, as in business matters, so it fits an adjective

parts.note: eco is the short prefix for environmentally green

indicators.note: in a down clue, rising says these pieces are read upwards, so reversed

parts.note: C is the chemical symbol for carbon
taken as written
on means about, concerning

explanation.surface: Rising carbon emissions mean someone backs green business.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to support' puts ECO above the reversed C, IM, ON (giving NOMIC) in the down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Economic means relating to trade, finance and commerce, the matters of business.

clue.text: Intimate German noun censor has camouflaged

indicators.note: camouflaged things are concealed within their surroundings, so the letters lie unseen inside these words

explanation.surface: A censor conceals a German noun that hints at something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Intimate' is the verb meaning to make known, not the adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: To intimate is to state or declare, especially to make known formally.

clue.text: Aunt Clare got staggering praise

indicators.note: staggering means lurching unsteadily, so these letters are thrown about into a new order

explanation.surface: A tipsy aunt receives compliments as she sways about.
explanation.definitionFit: To congratulate someone is to commend them for an achievement, giving them praise.

clue.text: Creatively representing us, do it here?

definitions.text: Creatively representing us, do it here?

indicators.note: representing something creatively recasts it in a new form, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An artist depicting people inventively asks whether this is the place to do it.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the anagram and the definition: an artist's workroom is where one would portray people creatively.
explanation.definitionFit: A studio is an artist's or photographer's workroom, where creative portraits are made.

clue.text: With little water, right to tuck into liquid daily

indicators.note: tucking into something means slipping inside it, so one piece goes within the other
liquid means fluid, not fixed, so the letters of daily flow into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone is entitled to their daily drink, though there is hardly any water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'liquid' rearranges DAILY to ADILY, and 'to tuck into' puts R inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Arid means dry and parched, so aridly describes a state of scarce moisture.

clue.text: Not a person that fails to finish in time

indicators.note: failing to finish means stopping short, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: not a single person is no one

explanation.surface: Nobody who fails to complete the task on schedule.
explanation.definitionFit: Midday, twelve o'clock, is a particular time of day.

clue.text: A spinning top is one's pick-me-up

definitions.text: A spinning top is one's pick-me-up

parts.words: A spinning top is one's pick-me-up
parts.note: a rotating blade on top is what lifts this aircraft, which can also pick people up and carry them off

explanation.surface: A child's spinning top is a cheering tonic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spinning top' suggests a toy and 'pick-me-up' a tonic; literally a rotor on top and an aircraft that lifts people up.
explanation.definitionFit: The aircraft is lifted by rotating blades mounted on its roof and is used for airlifts and rescues.

clue.text: Funding part of UK — that's upset another country

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset turns these pieces upside down, so they read in reverse

parts.note: aid is funding or financial help
NI is Northern Ireland, part of the United Kingdom

explanation.surface: Money for one part of the UK has offended a different nation.
explanation.definitionFit: India is a nation in South Asia, distinct from the UK already mentioned.

clue.text: Feline figure seen within banks of lagoon

indicators.note: seen within means appearing inside, so the next piece sits between the edges
the banks of something are its edges, so the first and last letters are taken

parts.note: the figure 10 resembles the letters I and O

explanation.surface: A cat-like shape is spotted by the shores of a lagoon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'figure' is the number 10, written as the letters IO.
explanation.definitionFit: The lion is a big cat, one of the felines.

clue.text: Declared hands with ace, diamonds, holding it back

indicators.note: holding means containing, so these pieces wrap around the next

parts.note: hands are workers, men
an ace counts as one
D is the card-game abbreviation for diamonds

indicators.note: back says the word it is reversed

explanation.surface: A card player announces their hand, with an ace of diamonds held back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hands', 'ace' and 'diamonds' suggest a card game, but hands are workmen; 'back' turns the pronoun round and 'holding' sets it in the middle.
explanation.definitionFit: To have mentioned something is to have stated or referred to it, so declared.

clue.text: A trio of Democrats taking ecstasy carried on

indicators.note: taking in means admitting, so the next piece goes inside

parts.note: three Ds, D being the abbreviation for Democrat
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: Three politicians on drugs kept going.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taking' places E between the second and third D.
explanation.definitionFit: To carry on talking is to continue, as one who added a further remark, 'he went on'.

clue.text: Wiped part of article, an editorial

indicators.note: part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A newspaper item where part of an editorial has been erased.
explanation.definitionFit: Wiping a surface removes dirt from it, making it clean.

clue.text: Everyone needs some organisation

parts.note: any means some, an unspecified amount
a body is an organisation, as in a governing body

explanation.surface: Everyone needs to belong to some institution.
explanation.definitionFit: In 'anybody can do it', the word means every person without exception, so everyone.
